newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Land news propels SIMEX Nikkei to strong close.
newsitem.headline: Land news propels SIMEX Nikkei to strong close.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures were lifted out of the doldrums and ended sharply up on Tuesday on news Japan's government would announce details of measures to improve liquidity in the stagnant land market on March 31.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract added 410 points to close at 18,465, just 20 points off an intra-day high. Market turnover was relatively light at 16,390 lots.

"It was all based on the land liquidity scheme today," said a Japanese bank dealer. He said the Nikkei stood to benefit further if the Finance Ministry went ahead with a proposal to scrap taxes on securities transactions.
The Finance Ministry said in January it would discuss the abolition of the tax as part of an overall reform of Japan's tax system, planned for the year from April 1, 1998.
"If the June Nikkei closes above the topside of 18,600 this week, I would say this market is definitely on the way up," the dealer said.

Yamaichi Securities and Bank of Ikeda's downward revisions of their 1996/97 earnings forecasts after the market's close were unlikely to dampen sentiment as players had already discounted such news ahead of the financial year end on March 31, he added.
A chartist with a local institution said the June Nikkei was likely to undergo a short-term correction before heading higher to test resistance at 18,655.
"At worst, we'll probably come off to 18,000. After that, I feel there's more upside and the market could make an attempt to break today's high," he said.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 364.1 against its opening 361.6 on volume of 773 lots.
